title: How Used Engine Oil Can Get Re-Refined And Become Usable Again
raw_summary: If you're like us, you've made several trips to AutoZone or some other auto parts store to turn in your used motor oil after changing it. Or maybe you've watched the techs at the quick-lube place drain your used oil into one of their big barrels. What happens to that oil? What do they do with it? Well, some of it — as much as 20% according to some estimates – gets refined and is used as motor oil or some other lubricant again. The end product is literally as good as new. summary: If you're like us, you've made several trips to AutoZone or some other auto parts store to turn in your used motor oil after changing it. Or maybe you've watched the techs at the quick-lube place drain your used oil into one of their big barrels.
article_paragraphs: If you're like us, you've made several trips to AutoZone or some other auto parts store to turn in your used motor oil after changing it. Or maybe you've watched the techs at the quick-lube place drain your used oil into one of their big barrels. What happens to that oil? What do they do with it? Well, some of it — as much as 20% according to some estimates – gets refined and is used as motor oil or some other lubricant again. The end product is literally as good as new.

Safety-Kleen's Fallon Refinery can process 28 million gallons of used oil per year. It is turned into such products as base oil which can be further refined into motor oil, vacuum gas oil, V401 industrial fuels, and asphalt. That refinery runs around 80,000 gallons of used motor oil a day, which it refines into about 55,000 gallons of vacuum gas oil which, in turn, is used to make base oil.

The benefits of re-refining used motor oil speak for themselves. And getting your used oil recycled is easy . However, did you know it takes one gallon of used motor oil to make 2.5 quarts of usable lubricating oil? That may sound like a lot, but it takes 42 gallons of crude oil to make the same 2.5 quarts. That's not to say the rest of the oil is put to waste. It's normally used for other petroleum-based products. Still, it's apparent how much more efficient it is to refine used motor oil than crude.

Dirty oil is pretty easy to spot. The dark or black oil that comes out of your oil pan during an oil change looks a lot different from the honey-colored semi-clear lubricant you poured into the engine. By that time, your car's oil has been contaminated with all kinds of gnarly things , like dirt, metal, water, and chemicals. Those contaminants can mess up your car , which is why we do oil changes. But that doesn't mean the hydrocarbon molecules that give the oil its lubricating qualities can't be salvaged. That's where refining comes in.

Re-refining requires several steps, some of which may vary by refiner. In Stay-Kleene's case, the first step is for the oil to be screened for any contaminating chemicals which would interfere with it being refined. Then, any water is evaporated away. Light fuels and glycol are then separated, and the glycol eventual gets refined into another product. Heavy and middleweight fuels are then stripped, resulting in fuels for industrial heating. Heavy materials are removed by a process called vacuum distillation, leaving heavy oil which can be used for applications like asphalt extenders. Hydrogen is used to purge what's left of the used oil of contaminants like sulfer, nitrogen, chlorine, and heavy metals. The end result is a super clean base oil. Once additives are blended in, it's ready for the shelf. According to the EPA, refined used oil is as good as the newly refined stuff.

There are numerous benefits of re-refining used motor oil. In fact, it's the EPA's preferred way of recycling oil. But, as we stated before, some say only 20% of used motor oil ends up getting re-refined. Why such a relatively small amount? Not every oil collection spot is near a re-refinery. Some used oil gets mixed with harmful chemicals. The cost of re-refining can be high, especially when it comes to the initial investment in equipment and constructing facilities.

So, what happens to used motor oil that is not re-refined? There are other ways to recycle used motor oil, though they don't have all the upsides of re-refining. For example, contaminants can be removed from used oil on site. But without additives, the oil is not the same quality as brand-new, though it does last longer. Another way used oil can be recycled is that it can be used for feedstock at refineries, where it is made into other petroleum products. A lot of used motor oil is burned for fuel in industrial settings or as heating oil after water and other particulates are removed.

Unfortunately, a lot of used motor oil is dumped on the ground or in water or thrown in the trash. Just a quarter-gallon of oil can contaminate 250,000 gallons of water, and even oil dumped on the ground or in landfills can seep into ground water. So, don't dump it; just take it to a nearby auto parts store that will handle it.

raw_title: Trump’s War on Iran Has Broken the Oil Market
title: Trump’s War on Iran Has Broken the Oil Market
raw_summary: Almost 8 months into Trump’s war on Iran, we can see more clearly the consequences of this quagmire. Some have been quite unexpected, like the surprising resilience of the oil market, the emergence of multiple failure points outside of Hormuz (including Bab-al Mandeb, the East-West pipeline, and global refinery capacity), and the increased risk of regionalization for the conflict. These issues have no doubt taken a lot of analysts by surprise. Others, like Trump’s reluctance to admit he messed up, have been quite expected.
summary: Almost 8 months into Trump’s war on Iran, we can see more clearly the consequences of this quagmire. Some have been quite unexpected, like the surprising resilience of the oil market, the emergence of multiple failure points outside of Hormuz (including Bab-al Mandeb, the East-West pipeline, and global refinery capacity), and the increased risk of regionalization for the conflict.
article_paragraphs: Almost 8 months into Trump’s war on Iran, we can see more clearly the consequences of this quagmire. Some have been quite unexpected, like the surprising resilience of the oil market, the emergence of multiple failure points outside of Hormuz (including Bab-al Mandeb, the East-West pipeline, and global refinery capacity), and the increased risk of regionalization for the conflict. These issues have no doubt taken a lot of analysts by surprise.
Others, like Trump’s reluctance to admit he messed up, have been quite expected.

But today I want to talk about something else. I believe this war has either caused or displayed a seismic change in the way global oil markets work. I believe that for the first time since oil is a thing, oil demand is becoming elastic.
And since so far I haven’t seen anyone make this claim, I wanted to put my hypothesis up for debate.
When speaking about demand, economists normally use the terms elastic and inelastic to determine how much consumption will fluctuate when prices go up or down.

Some things, such as food staples, are consumed at quite stable levels. People will keep eating roughly the same regardless of their economic situation (unless very, very dire), and likewise, people who become wealthier are unlikely to eat much more: someone who just got a job paying double is not going to suddenly buy twice as many potatoes. This means that food demand is considered inelastic. Keep in mind this works the other way around: if potatoes suddenly halve in price, it’s unlikely that someone will suddenly start eating double the amount of them.
(I apologize to all the economists reading this if my examples are too simple or otherwise dumb, but these were the best ideas I had in mind.)

For a very, very long time, oil demand has been considered inelastic. Since people need to commute to their jobs, visit their relatives, and move products around regardless of income or oil prices, oil consumption has remained roughly constant (with a tendency to increase over time), with demand increasing a bit faster if oil is cheap and a bit slower if oil is expensive. In this context, oil demand has historically required an economic crisis to go down: either the economy slows down for unrelated reasons and oil demand falls with economic activity generally (as happened during the 2008 subprime crisis), or oil prices go up so much that they cause a recession, only falling back down again through reduced economic activity (as happened during the 1973 and 1979 oil crisis).

summary: There are very few cars that are as closely associated with affordable mass-motoring as the original Volkswagen Beetle. The famously rear-engine, rear-wheel-drive Type 1, as it was known internally, entered series production way back in 1945. No fewer than 21.5 million units later, production finally wrapped up in 2003.
article_paragraphs: There are very few cars that are as closely associated with affordable mass-motoring as the original Volkswagen Beetle. The famously rear-engine, rear-wheel-drive Type 1, as it was known internally, entered series production way back in 1945. No fewer than 21.5 million units later, production finally wrapped up in 2003.

Despite enjoying a near-60-year-long career, the Beetle's underpinnings went through very little in the way of revolution over that time. The air-cooled flat-four engine remained rear-mounted for the entirety of production, although Volkswagen did experiment with at least one water-cooled prototype , and the recipe was tweaked as the years marched on.

Initially, the flat-four boasted just 22.5 horsepower from a capacity of only 985 cubic centimeters, although later iterations saw that capacity grow to 1.1-, 1.2-, 1.3-, 1.5-, and finally 1.6-liter versions. Power rose in the Brazilian-market 1.2- and 1.3-liter variants to a peak of 45 gross hp, while the 1.5-liter saw that swell to 52 gross hp. It grew higher still with the 1.6-liter four, with the Brazilian-market 1974 Fusca 1600 seeing the Beetle's time-tested flat-four engine reach its peak gross rating of 65 hp. It was the use of twin carburetors that allowed the Fusca 1600 to achieve such an output, making it the most powerful original Beetle in a factory state. The implementation of dual-port cylinder heads in 1970 had also assisted Volkswagen in its pursuit of improved performance.

However, performance was never the Beetle's primary goal, so it should come as no surprise to read that its air-cooled four never exceeded the dizzying heights of 65 gross horses. Its core purpose remained solving mass-market transportation problems, with motivation provided by a simple, easy-to-service, easy-to-repair flat-four.

While the Beetle did originally start off with a dinky 985 cc engine, that engine never made it into Beetle series production. When production officially began in the post-war years, the engine size had grown slightly to 1,131 cc, and power sat at 25 horses. These units also featured engine and transmission housings cast from Elektron, an alloy of roughly 90% magnesium, for lightness, but the real changes were to come from '54 onward.

That year, 1,192 cc engines were introduced. Early versions gave just 30 hp, while engines of this displacement from '60 onward saw cylinder head work implemented too, which netted owners a few valuable extra horses. Still, at just 34 hp, the Beetle was far from a performance machine, and customer demands left Volkswagen looking at a displacement increase once more.

A 1.3-liter engine was introduced in 1965 and was soon followed in '66 by the 1.5-liter. It was very similar to the earlier 1.2-liter units in its construction, but power had now increased to 44 horses. Fast-forward to the '70 model year, and the U.S. market received the 57-hp single-port 1.6-liter engine, followed by the '71 model year's 60-horse dual-port 1.6-liter lump (both gross figures). Just a few short years later, Brazil's '74 Fusca 1600 would arrive, realizing the peak of Type 1 performance. Over the years, the engine was constantly tweaked in order to survive, gaining things like market-specific altitude sensors to improve air-fuel ratios , electronic ignition, and fuel injection systems.

No fewer than 21.5 million units later, production finally wrapped up in 2003.

article_paragraphs: If you're not already using microfiber towels to dry or clean your car , you should start. They're not only much softer and more absorbent than traditional sponges, but also readily available, inexpensive, and effective for drying paint, cleaning windows, and detailing interiors. However, they require care, and if they get dirty, you'd be wise to retire them.

Microfiber towels are usually made out of tiny strands of polyester. The thickness of these strands can vary significantly depending on the quality of the towel, with some having strands 1/100 th the diameter of a normal human hair. A single square inch of one of these towels can pack more than 200,000 fibers.

These tiny fibers are perfect for picking up dirt, grime, and gunk that builds up on a car's exterior and interior, so it's no surprise why they are the go-to for car detailers around the world. Microfiber towels are especially useful for drying a car, as a single large, high-quality towel can dry an entire car without risking damage. They are also much safer on paint than traditional chamois, or shammy, cloths.

The downside of using a microfiber towel is that it can pick up unwanted dirt. If you accidentally drop a microfiber towel while washing or drying your car, it's very likely to pick up microscopic pieces of rock or sand from the ground. If you then use that towel on your car's delicate paintwork, there's a good chance you'll create a bunch of swirl marks that'll glisten in the sun and detract from your car's overall look.

You can safely wash microfiber towels in your washing machine, and many companies even sell dedicated detergents designed specifically for them to remove oils, waxes, and polishes. However, not even fancy detergents are guaranteed to remove all the debris a towel may pick up from the pavement. So, if you drop a towel, it's best to throw it away immediately. If you keep using it, you'll likely damage your paint and leave scratches that only a professional detailer can remove.

If that sounds a little wasteful, a simple alternative is to use these towels elsewhere. Microfiber towels clean shower screens or benchtops just as well as they do a car's paint, so moving them from your garage to your kitchen could be a good idea. Alternatively, you can use older microfiber towels to detail a car's interior , such as wiping down door panels and dashboards. Just as we'd recommend against using dirty ones on your car's exterior, it's also wise to keep them away from interior screens, as dirt and sand can be incredibly abrasive.
bullet_points: If you're not already using microfiber towels to dry or clean your car , you should start.
They're not only much softer and more absorbent than traditional sponges, but also readily available, inexpensive, and effective for drying paint, cleaning windows, and detailing interiors.
However, they require care, and if they get dirty, you'd be wise to retire them.

raw_summary: Ferrari completed a full set of top United States Grand Prix Formula 1 practice times in the final session at Austin, though a track limits deletion for Charles Leclerc meant this time it was Lewis Hamilton on top. Ferrari had also been on top during the longer runs in the first part of the session before teams switched to qualifying simulations.
Hamilton expressed his frustration with Gabriel Bortoleto over a traffic incident - one of quite a few in the session - that will be looked at by the stewards.

Leclerc was far from the only driver to fall foul of track limits as the wild number of laptime deletions continued through the session. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli and both McLaren drivers were among the other high-profile transgressors.

Though Leclerc's lap loss meant Red Bull ended the session second with Verstappen, both he and Isack Hadjar had plenty of complaints over team radio and Verstappen having a wild lock-up, slide and wheelspin moment to end his session.

Alex Albon also received Hadjar's team radio ire - albeit for an 'impeding' incident that looked like it only happened because a big mistake from Hadjar carried him towards the slower-moving Williams.
The laptime deletions helped Nico Hulkenberg to get Audi as high as seventh, splitting the McLarens.

The new ID. Unyx 09 has a range of 755 km (469 miles) according to the CLTC rating system, and ranges from 179,900 yuan ($26,939) for the Ultra version to 249,900 yuan ($37,421) for the Max version (and in between them is the Flagship version for 219,900 yuan/$32,929). You can get it as a single-motor sedan or a dual-motor sedan, with the model falling into the midsize class or the large sedan class depending on who you ask.

“The ID. Unyx 09’s front fascia features a closed grille, slim headlights, and the iconic Volkswagen logo. High-tech lighting features include DLP high-definition matrix projection headlights and crystal laser-engraved interactive LED units, which can project lane-guidance light carpets and vehicle-width markers to enhance nighttime safety,” CarNewsChina shares.

The vehicle is powered by the VLA large-model intelligent driving assistance system, supporting advanced features such as custom parking, remote parking, and trace-back reversing.” That VLA (Vision-Language-Action) system comes courtesy of XPENG.
The car also includes a 91.963 kWh lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) battery from CATL, 5C ultra-fast charging, and a dual-chamber air suspension system.

What do you think? Can it sell well in China? Can it help spur on a revival for Volkswagen in the largest car market in the world? And, oh, by the way, can we get that car somewhere outside of China at some point?

article_paragraphs: Removing the roof rack crossbars from you vehicle can improve your fuel economy

With fuel prices continually weighing on drivers' wallets , squeezing every possible mile out of a tank of gas is more of a priority than ever before. Common fuel-saving advice includes being light-footed on the gas pedal and monitoring the tire pressure from time to time. While those steps certainly help, other factors deserve equal attention, including a popular accessory sitting directly above your head that could be quietly costing you money in the long run.

If you haven't guessed by now, we are talking about roof racks. Automakers spend millions of dollars fine-tuning vehicle aerodynamics, but practicality demands and aftermarket trends often compromise that work by significantly worsening a vehicle's drag coefficient.

We all know that crossbars and cargo boxes are undeniably useful for longer road trips, family vacations, and camping adventures. However, if you keep driving your daily with an unused roof rack , you effectively impose a continuous tax on your efficiency.

The main issue with roof racks and pretty much any other exterior add-on is the inevitable increase in aerodynamic drag, although weight could also play its role. Roof-mounted accessories not only increase the frontal area but also interrupt the smooth airflow over the vehicle, causing turbulence.

Physics taught us that these negative effects become far more pronounced at highway speeds. Meanwhile, even factory accessories with an aerodynamically optimized shape can take a heavy toll on overall efficiency.

A few years ago, our colleagues at Car and Driver discovered that removing the factory crossbars from their Kia Carnival press car delivered an instant improvement, bumping real-world fuel economy from 25 to 28 mpg. As a result, the minivan's highway range expanded by a full 60 miles (97 km).

In another test conducted by Consumer Reports , a Nissan Altima sedan suffered an 11% drop (5 mpg) in fuel economy at 65 mph (105 km/h) when a roof rack was installed. When combined with a roof carrier box, the efficiency toll increased to 19% (9 mpg). The effects proved to be less dramatic in a boxier SUV, but driving without a roof rack will always save you gas money.

raw_title: This Tractor Supply Mini Bike Will Help Awaken Your Inner Child
title: This Tractor Supply Mini Bike Will Help Awaken Your Inner Child
raw_summary: Motorcycles are awesome. We all know it. Even your protective parents who cautioned you against a life on two wheels likely understand why motorcyclists trade safety for satisfaction. Sometimes, for safety reasons, financial reasons, or other such rationale, we don't take our moto-ambitions on the road. However, that doesn't mean you have to live a life devoid of motorcycle fun. If you're okay with keeping your rides off-road and full of childlike whimsy, there might be a solution for you at your local Tractor Supply . You can get all sorts of stuff at this massive retail store, but you may not have expected the agricultural and rural retailer to sell you a pocket-sized motorcycle. We're talking about the Massimo MB 200, a one-cylinder trail-going mini bike — though it's practically hulking compared to what may very well be the smallest Ducati ever made . While you can't slap a license plate on the thing, it looks as though it would be right at home conquering grassy fields and muddy trails. Right now, the MB 200 is on sale in five different colors and ships to most U.S. states. It's light, cartoonish, and takes a no-frills, back-to-the-basics approach to off-road riding. No clutching, no front brake, and not even a legitimate gas tank; just the essentials for a riotous ride. Better yet, the little sub-$1000 toy motorbike doesn't break the bank.

No clutching, no front brake, and not even a legitimate gas tank; just the essentials for a riotous ride. Better yet, the little sub-$1000 toy motorbike doesn't break the bank.

Massimo is no stranger to making teeny tiny versions of awesome stuff for full-size operators. The brand sells miniature Jeep lookalikes and even a new mini truck that channels adult Power Wheels energy at Tractor Supply . That's not all the Texas-based brand does, though. It's primarily an off-road vehicle manufacturer, rolling out American-made UTVs and ATVs. Still, Massimo also has an odd little collection of toy-ish vehicles, including a couple of pull-start mini bikes.

It's a simple package: At a glance, the MB 200 looks like one of those classic little Lego motorcycles blown up to rideable proportions. As you might imagine, then, it's light — just 154 pounds of dry weight. No two-stroke antics, either. This thing is powered by 6.5-hp a 196-cc four-stroke single-cylinder engine connected to a centrifugal clutch automatic gearbox. How fast is the little Massimo mini bike? The manufacturer says the carbureted and air-cooled motorbike is rated for 24 miles per hour. That's about 4 mph shy of how quick you can go in one of the brand's $3,000 mini trucks.

Front brakes? Who needs them? The MB 200 has a pull-cable disc rear brake to bring the mini motorcycle to a halt. The 40-inch-tall motorcycle rides on a 19-inch set of knobby all-terrain tires and features no rear suspension unless on the standard model. In front of the rider, the diminutive Massimo also has no gauges. The apparent fuel tank ahead of the rider isn't really a tank; it's storage. See? No frills, all fun.

As of this writing, the MB 200 is advertised for $999 on Tractor Supply's website . That sales price applies to every one of the Massimo mini bike's five color options: Black, Red, Tactical Gray, Quicksand, and Camo. Depending on where you live, you might not have access to the full helping of colors at your local Tractor Supply. For instance, you simply can't get an MB 200 finished in the camouflage colorway in North Carolina right now — shipped or picked up in-store. Tractor Supply also includes a notice that the silly little trail toy can't be delivered to Alaska, Arkansas, California, Idaho, Louisiana, Oregon, Washington, or West Virginia.

What if you want something with a bit more spring in its step? Massimo also builds the MB 200S, and aside from one extra horsepower, springs are primarily what sets the siblings apart. Unlike the MB 200 and its hardtail approach, the "S" model features a wee set of dual rear shocks. That said, the MB 200 S is also the smaller of the two, ditching 5 inches of wheelbase, 6 inches of overall length, and 0.8 inches of ground clearance compared to its mini bike brother. So you could get either one on your next trip to buy a new post hole digger, or you could try to build a go-kart out using only parts from Tractor Supply .

However, that doesn't mean you have to live a life devoid of motorcycle fun.

title: 7 Reasons The Death Of The Sedan Has Been Greatly Exaggerated
raw_summary: Jalopnik readers tell automakers to make more sedans , yet despite the obvious enthusiast demand, it felt for a while like the traditional four-door car was destined for a niche fate like station wagons and landline telephones. But something funny has happened on the way to the sedan's funeral: Americans are buying them again. They never really stopped, of course. Nobody considers the Camry and the Accord to be endangered species, but on the other hand, we have other manufacturers abandoning the segment completely. Sales figures from 2026 have shown interest in sedans on the uptick across multiple brands and price ranges. article_paragraphs: Jalopnik readers tell automakers to make more sedans , yet despite the obvious enthusiast demand, it felt for a while like the traditional four-door car was destined for a niche fate like station wagons and landline telephones. But something funny has happened on the way to the sedan's funeral: Americans are buying them again.

They never really stopped, of course. Nobody considers the Camry and the Accord to be endangered species, but on the other hand, we have other manufacturers abandoning the segment completely. Sales figures from 2026 have shown interest in sedans on the uptick across multiple brands and price ranges. The crossoverfication of the market will likely continue, but perhaps reports of the sedan's inevitable demise have been overstated.

This shift is obviously welcome, but today we're going to dig into what may be behind it, what's going on with SUVs, and whether the year's lift in sales is an anomalous blip or the beginning of a sedan resurgence.

For a minute there, it felt like every bit of automotive news about the American sedan market was about another model being discontinued, a factory switching over to SUV production, or an automaker explaining why nobody wants a regular car anymore. Sales figures for the first nine months of 2026 tell a different story, however. The Toyota Camry sold 260,684 units through September, up 11.2% over the same period in 2025. The Honda Accord was up even more, with a 32.7% increase. What about down market? The Corolla was up 8.4% and the Civic by 5.4%. These aren't obscure enthusiast darlings. They were once the bread and butter of the entire car market, now showing some momentum again.

These numbers are interesting, but they wouldn't necessarily mean a whole lot in isolation. If you take Honda as an example, though, passenger cars in general were up by 16.5% through September, while trucks and SUVs were essentially flat, actually declining by 0.3%. It's almost like sedans are poised to make a comeback . But why?

One of the big reasons why sedans may be gaining traction again has nothing to do with sedans. Conventional wisdom has long held that Americans were willing to pay extra for the privilege of sitting really high in traffic. But a market where the cheapest new full-sized SUVs start at more than $60,000 , combined with an economic crunch that has become hard to ignore, is making SUV math look more and more unappealing.

Kelley Blue Book data helps show just how stark the choice has become. Looking at transaction prices, the cost of a new compact car has been $27,977 on average. To step up into a compact SUV, that average jumps to $37,614. For a mid-size SUV, it's $50,630. We aren't talking about full-sized SUVs that dramatically increase seating and cargo capacity for that money, so buyers are paying that sort of premium for a vehicle configuration that's potentially very similar.

Cars actually asked Hyundai about this, and the brand confirmed that affordability was driving this shift, with fuel economy and the overall perception of value playing roles as well. So, while a sedan may sit lower and offer a bit less space inside, it's also delivering a lower price tag and better gas mileage without asking anyone to give up a trunk and a proper back seat.

title: Gary Anderson's simple design solution for F1's impeding problem
raw_summary: Every Formula 1 race weekend, there are constant complaints about drivers being blocked when on a fast lap. Expect more when United States Grand Prix qualifying happens later today. Yet there is a simple solution that could be implemented immediately to prevent these near-misses.
summary: Every Formula 1 race weekend, there are constant complaints about drivers being blocked when on a fast lap. Expect more when United States Grand Prix qualifying happens later today. Yet there is a simple solution that could be implemented immediately to prevent these near-misses.
article_paragraphs: Every Formula 1 race weekend, there are constant complaints about drivers being blocked when on a fast lap. Expect more when United States Grand Prix qualifying happens later today.
Yet there is a simple solution that could be implemented immediately to prevent these near-misses.

The extent of the problem is obvious. There have been stewards’ investigations into impeding on 12 out of 17 race weekends already this year, with a total of 14 punishments issued, some of those grid penalties. And even when it doesn’t go this far, the airwaves are filled with drivers complaining about being held up over the radio.
This doesn’t need a complicated fix that requires you to reinvent the wheel or spend huge amounts of money. It doesn’t even need something new to be added.
Simply change the regulations to double the size of the rear-view mirrors and more closely define the ideal position for those.
By 'ideal' I don’t mean aerodynamically ideal - I mean for the driver’s line of sight.

To give an idea of the size, I’ve highlighted what I would do in white on the Mercedes in the image on the right. You can see the comparison to the current standard size mirrors on the Red Bull on the left.
Yes, it will create a little more drag and make the aero design more difficult, but it’s more important to reduce the number of times qualifying is changed by impeding.

title: Chinese EVs found back door into Western car markets – at 40% off MSRP

article_paragraphs: The dumb oil war in Iran is driving up the cost of just about everything , including new cars. That’s giving Chinese EVs a huge advantage over Western “legacy” car brands already lagging in tech and struggling with affordability – and those legacy brands about to have a whole new to them problem on their hands: USED Chinese EVs .

Western automakers have leaned on protectionist trade policies to keep cheaper Chinese rivals at bay, placing strict limits on the number of new Chinese cars allowed in and hefty tariffs on new battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) are as high as 45.3% in the EU. That supply limitation is, of course, ratcheting up demand for the high-tech, low-cost Chinese machines, and buyers in Europe and Canada are finding that used Chinese EVs – which offer comparable tech to the newest Western EVs, a price tag up to 40% lower than their already low MSRPs, and which are not subject to the same protectionist import duties – are a workable alternative.
According to data shared by importers/exporters China EV Marketplace ( CEVM ), pre-owned vehicle sales to EU customers grew 280% year over year, with sales climbing to 7,900 units through September.

“Tariffs have already weakened demand for new Chinese BEVs among our European customers. We expect the hybrid import cap to put pressure on new PHEV sales too,” CEVM COO Jakub Geršl told CarNewsChina . “Pre-owned cars are exempt from the additional BEV tariffs and from the new hybrid (PHEV) quota. That is why we are making pre-owned vehicles the main focus of our European business.”

CEVM has more than 2,600 used Chinese EVs on its website as I type this, and their inventory is refreshed almost daily with fresh pre-owned examples of cars from brands like BYD, Geely, Zeekr, and others – and the company claims its prices are about 40% below the original price (MSRP) on average.

“Lower new-car prices put pressure on pre-owned prices as well,” Geršl adds. “Our Shanghai-based team searches for those opportunities. We regularly find cars with around 6,000 km on the clock priced 40% below their original Chinese list price.”

That price reduction is driven by a number of factors, including the relentless march of technological progress, the flood of new and updated EVs coming out of Chinese car brands, and a burgeoning domestic Chinese car culture that values newness above all else. If you’re reading between the lines there, I think you’ll find that that means more low-mileage, low-price, high-tech, and high-value Chinese EVs are coming to the West – and probably a lot sooner than brands like VW, who are struggling to compete as it is , would want.

And that’s the real problem – whether you agree with him or not, Elon Musk will tell you that technology and markets move faster than legislation , and once consumers go electric, precious few of them ever go back to gas or diesel , regardless of what that dude filming himself wearing PitVipers in the drivers’ seat of his pickup and your racist uncle on Facebook are telling you.

title: NHTSA proposes cyan lights for robotaxis, following Mercedes/China
raw_summary: The NHTSA has proposed using cyan-colored lights to identify vehicles operating autonomously, along with other additions to get ready for autonomous vehicles. As the autonomous vehicles start to spread on US roads, questions have come up about how to deal with these new driverless vehicles.
summary: The NHTSA has proposed using cyan-colored lights to identify vehicles operating autonomously, along with other additions to get ready for autonomous vehicles. As the autonomous vehicles start to spread on US roads, questions have come up about how to deal with these new driverless vehicles.
article_paragraphs: The NHTSA has proposed using cyan-colored lights to identify vehicles operating autonomously, along with other additions to get ready for autonomous vehicles.
As the autonomous vehicles start to spread on US roads, questions have come up about how to deal with these new driverless vehicles.

One question involves emergency response – not only do the vehicles need to be prepared to respond to emergency personnel, those personnel need to recognize when a car is operating autonomously. A police officer needs to know that nobody’s in the driver seat, or an emergency responder needs to know that if there’s nobody in the driver’s seat, that’s not necessarily because there’s a missing driver somewhere who needs rescue.
These are just some of the reasons one might want to know whether a car is operating autonomously, but as of yet, there is no standardized messaging to suggest that a vehicle is doing so.
This week, NHTSA proposed an answer. In a draft proposal released Friday , it suggested a whole new color for vehicle lamps, cyan, to signal autonomous operation.

The proposal was actually first put forward by Mercedes, alongside its DRIVE PILOT level 3 driver assist system. This is the first true hands-free system offered in the US, which allows drivers to forgo responsibility for the car under certain conditions, and let the car truly drive itself. This differs from systems like Tesla’s Full Self-Driving, which is actually only a “level 2” system, where the driver is still responsible when the system is on.
We tried Mercedes’ system out in Santa Monica traffic , and were impressed at how quickly we adjusted to our temporary robotic chauffer.
When we saw that system, we also saw Mercedes’ proposal for lighting: cyan lights around the exterior of the vehicle, denoting autonomous operation.

Launching with an initial cohort of 17 key suppliers, Chain Reaction delivers collaborative enablement across four pillars:

In fiscal year 2026, Logitech already achieved a 33% reduction in its total Scope 3 carbon footprint compared to its 2021 baseline 1 . Chain Reaction builds on this momentum by empowering suppliers to identify carbon hotspots and execute practical engineering solutions directly within their facilities and supply chains.

“Real value-chain decarbonization happens directly on the factory floor,” said Elaine Laird, chief people and sustainability officer at Logitech. “Our suppliers understand their operations best. Chain Reaction helps our manufacturing partners access the practical tools, technical evaluations and clean energy solutions they need to optimize their operations and lead their own decarbonization roadmaps.”

To support participating facilities, the program provides technical workshops on establishing GHG baselines, direct access to subject matter experts and pathways to pilot cutting-edge innovations through the Logitech Future Positive Challenge .

“By integrating carbon transparency and decarbonization progress into our commercial metrics, we are enabling more value for our suppliers to grow with Logitech,” said Sree Chenincherry, chief supply chain operations officer at Logitech. “From an operational standpoint, decarbonization and efficiency go hand-in-hand. Equipping our manufacturing partners to reduce energy waste and transition to clean power unlocks structural cost savings, mitigates long-term volatility and strengthens our entire shared value chain.”

Logitech creates design-led, software-enabled hardware solutions that help businesses thrive and bring people together when working, creating and gaming in the age of AI. article_paragraphs: Recent warnings from American AI leaders have created the impression that the world is only beginning to confront the dangers of advanced artificial intelligence.
Dario Amodei, chief executive of tech company Anthropic, has called for governments to intervene to slow the development of increasingly powerful AI models .
His proposal begins with independent evaluators embedded inside AI companies, moves on to regulation and progresses to government-backed coordination among democratic states.
Ultimately, it seeks global agreements with China on testing of AI systems, dangerous applications of the technology and the pace of AI development.
Yet there is a China-shaped hole in this narrative. The Asian superpower is portrayed as the difficult final participant in a governance system that the US and its allies must first create.

In fact, China has already established an extensive system of AI rules, assessment, filing, technical standards and government oversight. Here’s how China’s AI governance system has developed in stages alongside the technology itself.
Beijing’s 2022 rules on algorithmic recommendation services apply to technologies that select, rank, filter or recommend online content to users.

They compel companies that use algorithms to examine how they work, to protect the personal information of users, to give users certain controls, and to introduce safeguards for workers, consumers, children and older people.

article_paragraphs: I was intrigued by the recent announcement from Chery that they were going to import a diesel plugin hybrid ute to Australia.

With Australian highways abounding in diesel utes and petrol PHEVs (notably, the BYD Shark 6 and the Canon Alpha), why hasn’t this been done before? Carsguide touts the Chery Stockman diesel PHEV as not just a BYD competitor, but also a worthy challenger for the Ford Ranger.

It is difficult to find direct comparisons regarding the number of PHEV utes on Australian roads . The best I could do was the following: Although the data and time periods don’t totally match, they give the general direction of sales: From February 2025 to October 2026, BYD has sold 31,659 Shark 6 petrol hybrid utes. In the same time period, it appears that Great Wall (Canon Alpha PHEV) and Ford (Ranger PHEV) sold approximately the same numbers — possibly in the low thousands.
It should be noted that the Ford Ranger only has 30 km of electric range — about a third of its Chinese rivals.

The Shark 6 has taken a bite out of Toyota and Ford sales, but has been criticised for lack of towing and carrying power compared to diesel models. This has been somewhat rectified by the introduction of a performance version — however, it carries a higher cost. Will the Chery Stockman solve the towing, carrying, and cost factors? For the moment, it looks like towing and carrying are equal to the Shark Performance. As well as the electric range.

The Stockman diesel PHEV will be fitted with a 2.5 l turbo diesel as well as its electric motor. It will also be available as a petrol PHEV. Speculation is rife about pricing, with an expectation it will be priced to match the BYD Shark 6 (around AU$56,000). Reservations are now open, according to Chery’s official Australian webpage. You can see pictures here . “The Stockman does everything a serious ute should — hauls, tows, charges itself — and then somehow fits a luxury interior in there too. How? Honestly, don’t worry about it.” Echoes of a previous Queensland premier: “Don’t you worry about that.” Thanks, Joh. You can see him in action here .

Looking at Australia’s history with diesel utes, I was curious as to why a diesel PHEV has only just now been introduced. I have driven petrol cars for over 40 years, and at one point, we had three in the driveway. As life slowed down in retirement, we didn’t need all of those vehicles, but for the last few years we needed to keep them running. We called the cars Grace (Hyundai Sonata), Ruby (Hyundai Accent), and the grandfather of them all, George (a 1964 Wolseley). There were times when we just had to drive the car to make sure all the bits were working — “George/Ruby needs a run,” I would say.

I have never driven diesel, but my thinking is, if that is the case with petrol cars, what of diesel? What if I am using my new Chery Stockman diesel PHEV on electricity all the time for city commutes (I know, I know, who would do that?) and not using the diesel engine. Would that cause problems? I first turned to Professor Google to educate myself, and found this useful website .

article_paragraphs: TALLAHASSEE, Florida — On Tuesday, a life-size statue of Ron DeSantis began melting shortly after it was unveiled in front of supporters and onlookers in Tallahassee, an intentionally dramatic installation designed to make the consequences of climate change impossible to ignore.

The installation arrives ahead of the midterm elections and shortly after Climate Week NYC. Through the work, “DENIAL” is urging Americans to deny climate change deniers and sign a pledge to vote for climate conscious candidates. Sculpted entirely from gallium, a metal that melts at 85.6°F (29.8°C), “DENIAL” exposes the fragile illusion of performative politicians against the unyielding reality of the natural world. That melting point sits below Tallahassee’s average summer high, a threshold Florida will cross more often and for longer under 2°C of global heating.

The statue references DeSantis’s 2024 signing of HB 1645, which erased the phrase “climate change” from Florida state law — even as the state spent more than $1 billion responding to floods, storms, and heat. DeSantis is scheduled to leave office in January 2027 after serving eight years as governor and reaching his term limit.

“The climate crisis is one of the top issues facing our planet today. And yet, some candidates running for office still deny it’s happening, and deny the bold climate action that the people want,” said Candice Fortin, 350 Action Campaign Manager.

“That’s why it’s more important than ever to deny them back at the ballot box. If everyone who cares about people and our planet makes their voices heard on Election Day, we’ll be too loud to deny,” continued Fortin.

The statue was produced using 3D scanning and printing to achieve photorealistic detail, then cast in solid gallium, a metal that melts under the very conditions its subject legislated against acknowledging. As the record heat that has defined much of his tenure continues, DENIAL will not.
350 Action supports the bold, people-powered movements fighting to keep our planet livable. Learn more and get involved at 350action.org/denial.

About 350 Action: 350 Action is an organization that empowers voters to make a direct impact in the nation’s most important climate races. From local elections that decide energy policies to House races that could take Congress back from climate deniers, we support climate-progressive candidates and initiatives. Learn more at www.350action.org .

raw_title: This New Italian Sports Car Is The Closest Thing To A Modern Ferrari 308
title: This New Italian Sports Car Is The Closest Thing To A Modern Ferrari 308
raw_summary: Italian brand AC Motorsport has unveiled a modern take on the iconic Ferrari 308 , created in partnership with local engineering and racing car firm Michelotto. The car, badged the Michelotto Gruppo 4 Tributo, prioritizes a pure driving experience rather than earth-shattering performance like so many other new exotics. Francesco Calzavara founded AC Motorsport just two years ago after working at Michelotto. The Gruppo 4 Tributo looks very much like a restomodded 308 , but it's a new car built around a custom tubular chassis with lightweight composite panels. We'd argue Ferrari designers have lost their way in recent years, giving us odd-looking supercars like the 849 Testarossa and F80. By comparison, this 308 tribute looks just about perfect.
summary: Italian brand AC Motorsport has unveiled a modern take on the iconic Ferrari 308 , created in partnership with local engineering and racing car firm Michelotto. The car, badged the Michelotto Gruppo 4 Tributo, prioritizes a pure driving experience rather than earth-shattering performance like so many other new exotics.
article_paragraphs: Italian brand AC Motorsport has unveiled a modern take on the iconic Ferrari 308 , created in partnership with local engineering and racing car firm Michelotto. The car, badged the Michelotto Gruppo 4 Tributo, prioritizes a pure driving experience rather than earth-shattering performance like so many other new exotics.

Francesco Calzavara founded AC Motorsport just two years ago after working at Michelotto. The Gruppo 4 Tributo looks very much like a restomodded 308 , but it's a new car built around a custom tubular chassis with lightweight composite panels. We'd argue Ferrari designers have lost their way in recent years, giving us odd-looking supercars like the 849 Testarossa and F80. By comparison, this 308 tribute looks just about perfect.

The car's overall shape and footprint closely match the original. The nose sits low with a blacked-out grille, horizontal DRLs, and pop-up headlights. Just like a 308, there are also gills and vents on the hood and front quarter panels, though a set of flared fenders makes the Gruppo 4 Tributo look far more aggressive.

AC Motorsport and Michelotto have also nailed the design brief at the sides, crafting striking rocker panels, a large intake behind the doors, and a set of star-shaped wheels clad in Pirelli tires. The rear end is also much like the 308 and sports a huge clamshell, black grilles, dual exhausts, an exposed carbon fiber diffuser, and four circular taillights.

As impressive as the car's design is, it's the promised powertrain that has us really excited. The car features a naturally aspirated 3.4-liter V8 producing 380 horsepower and 269 pound-feet of torque, mated exclusively to a dog-leg manual transmission. While the peak horsepower and torque figures aren't extraordinary, the car's 950 kg curb weight (2,094 lbs) is worth celebrating. Modern cars are heavy, negatively impacting every performance metric. At 950 kg, the Gruppo 4 Tributo is 140 kg lighter than the original.

The car's interior is quite simple and, at least in this prototype, somewhat at odds with the exterior design. The dashboard is flat and carbon fiber, with a large screen in front of the driver and a bunch of physical switches and dials across the center. Other key features include a three-spoke steering wheel, a simple metal gated shifter, and carbon fiber racing seats. The cabin certainly isn't as stylish as the carbon fiber bodywork, but it at least seems functional.

Wondering where the car gets its name from? Well, the original Ferrari 308 GTB spawned several rally versions, including Group 4 specification models that were built by Michelotto and raced in the World Rally Championship. There's no word on when this new model will go on sale or how much it will cost.

title: Not Even A Partnership With Xpeng Can Save VW In China
raw_summary: Certain VW EVs are way off the mark when it comes to projected sales For years, China was Volkswagen's golden goose, serving as a crucial engine of growth that once accounted for almost 50% of the group's total profits. summary: Certain VW EVs are way off the mark when it comes to projected sales For years, China was Volkswagen's golden goose, serving as a crucial engine of growth that once accounted for almost 50% of the group's total profits. Now, that figure has fallen to roughly 10%, and it doesn't even look like the brand's flashy partnership with Xpeng can save it.
article_paragraphs: Certain VW EVs are way off the mark when it comes to projected sales

For years, China was Volkswagen's golden goose, serving as a crucial engine of growth that once accounted for almost 50% of the group's total profits. Now, that figure has fallen to roughly 10%, and it doesn't even look like the brand's flashy partnership with Xpeng can save it.

It's been more than three years since VW joined forces with Xpeng, spending $700 million to acquire a 4.99% stake in the Chinese brand. The two companies developed a dedicated electrical and electronics (E&E) architecture that underpinned several electrified vehicles, including the ID. Unyx 08 and ID. Unyx 09. By developing, designing, and building models in China for Chinese consumers, VW likely thought it had found the perfect recipe to remain relevant in the world's largest car market.

The figures indicate this isn't happening. Reuters reports that from April to August, monthly sales of the ID. Unyx 08 averaged just 267 vehicles. This represents less than 10% of VW's goal of selling up to 3,622 units each month. What's more, VW initially forecast selling 32,600 during 2026, up to 70,400 in 2027, and more than 120,000 units annually in the future. VW was forced to cut its 2026 goal to just 12,300 vehicles earlier this year and slashed the 2027 goal to 64,000. Both of those still seem extremely difficult to achieve.

Compared to VWs sold in Western markets, the ID. Unyx 08 has a radical new design and a tech-laden interior similar to many other new EVs in China, with expansive infotainment and passenger displays. However, customers have found it lacks the same technology as rivals like the Xiaomi YU7, and it doesn't offer fast charging to match the Zeekr 7X.

It appears VW also messed up its sales strategy. The ID. Unyx 08 has been sold primarily through the limited network of roughly 166 Volkswagen Anhui dealerships, and not the dealers it also operates with FAW and SAIC, which total more than 3,000.

While the ID. Unyx 08 hasn't proven to be the hit that VW was expecting, that doesn't mean it's winding down its ambitions in China. In fact, the brand thinks it can sell as many as 4,900 examples of the new ID. Unyx 09 sedan each and every month, and potentially sell as many as 90,000 annually by 2034. This low-slung sedan has a similar design to the ID. Unyx 08 and is available with the same 82-kWh and 95-kWh battery packs, as well as up to 496 horsepower. Like its SUV sibling, this model is entering a crowded segment, and it remains to be seen if it can pull customers away from popular models like the Tesla Model 3 and Xiaomi SU7.

While VW continues to navigate turbulent waters in China, it may be able to offset poor local demand for these models by selling them elsewhere. Earlier this year, it was reported that the brand was thinking about importing vehicles built in China to Europe , perhaps starting with the ID. Era 9X, which it builds alongside SAIC. The main issue with this plan is that these vehicles would face hefty tariffs. Vehicles from SAIC are currently hit with a 35% duty in addition to the EU's standard import tariff. One way to avoid these tariffs would be to build the vehicles in Europe, potentially at underutilized German factories. Doing so would require careful negotiations with the country's powerful IG Metall union.

title: Toyota Recalls 106K Hybrid Land Cruisers for Possible Fuel Leak
raw_summary: Gas is expensive these days, and filling up your SUV will cost you even more if it’s leaking fuel. That’s a potential concern for nearly 106K Land Cruiser owners, whose vehicles are involved in a new recall that Toyota has reported to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). The recall documents state that 105,794 hybrid Land Cruisers have a plastic fuel tube on the gas tank that connects to a metal fuel tube that sends the combustible liquid to the turbocharged four-cylinder engine. However, if the retaining clip that holds these two parts together is lifted, it can cause the fuel lines to disconnect and cause a leak. Not only will such a leak lead to wasted fuel and the gas engine eventually shutting off, but it also increases the risk of a fire.

While the recall covers over 105K Land Cruisers from the 2024 to 2027 model years, Toyota says that not all of the affected SUVs were sold in the United States. The automaker also hasn’t yet identified the cause of the issue, according to the NHTSA report. Still, Toyota says that all dealers have been notified about the recall, and all owners will be notified by mail by December 13, 2026. Toyota dealers have been instructed to inspect the fuel lines and install a supplemental clamp to prevent them from disconnecting, or to replace the plastic tube and install a clamp if necessary.

His aspiration growing up was to become a millionaire with a Jay Leno–like car collection. Apparently, getting rich is harder than social-media influencers make it seem, so he avoided financial success entirely to become an automotive journalist and drive new cars for a living. After earning a journalism degree at Central Michigan University and working at a daily newspaper, the years of basically burning money on failed project cars and lemon-flavored jalopies finally paid off when Car and Driver hired him. His garage currently includes a 2010 Acura RDX, a manual '97 Chevy Camaro Z/28, and a '90 Honda CRX Si.

In Japan’s Super Taikyu series, Toyota appears to be racing something in the middle form of a Yaris evolving into an MR2, as spotted by CarBuzz .

It’s called the Yaris M concept, and it’s a further developed prototype of the car of the same name that Toyota showed off at last year's Tokyo Auto Salon. Formerly just a Yaris hatchback shell with a turbocharged four-cylinder engine where the rear seats should be, the new Yaris M features full-on coupe bodywork with massive rear flares.

The silhouette isn't a complete surprise, as it’s a near match for Toyota’s 2027 WRC concept, which was spotted testing in Portugal this past spring. This Super Taikyu racer looks to be the tarmac version of that prototype.

The engine isn’t the GR Yaris’ frenetic little three-banger, but a new four-cylinder called the G20. Displacing 2.0 liters, it's turbocharged up to around 400 to 450 horsepower and has already proved its mettle in endurance racing.

Everyone who owned a second-generation MR2 Turbo has permission to start jumping up and down excitedly because this new car looks like a return of that particular F355-on-a-budget machine. Note also that one of the four drivers who will be campaigning the car in Super Taikyu is none other than Akio Toyota, using his Morizo nom de guerre.

While a potential return of one of Toyota’s 1990s performance heroes is something to get excited about all on its own, the further development of this G20 turbo four is no less intriguing. A reliable powerplant putting out 200 horsepower per liter of displacement could have all kinds of applications, including in the rumored return of the Celica as a replacement for the GR Corolla.

article_paragraphs: Three-time Emmy winner Aaron Paul has a blink and you’ll miss it cameo in the new DC movie Clayface . Now, the film’s director, James Watkins, has revealed why the Breaking Bad and Westworld star is in DC’s first R-rated horror movie.
Paul plays Jimmy “One Nut” Hagen, the late abusive father of protagonist Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries). Word of Paul’s casting was first reported by Feature First back in June.

Paul’s cameo occurs during the climactic action sequence set at the Gotham City nightclub Vesuvius where Matt confronts the gangsters who disfigured him. Matt finds the hood who killed his dad and morphs into his father to shock the killer.

Paul originally had a larger supporting role in Clayface, appearing in flashbacks to Matt’s youth, but the filmmakers ultimately cut nearly all of those scenes. Paul’s appearance in the nightclub is all that remains of his role.
“In terms of trying to figure out the character, it was, How much is Matt defined by his past and how much is he an everyman?” Watkins told Entertainment Weekly .

“At one point, we were looking at it and thinking, Is it the ‘sins of the father’? But actually, as we worked on the script, I thought that notion of revenge was more universal and more relatable to all of us. It doesn’t matter whether you’re carrying a trauma or any of that. If we’re slighted, we carry this sense of being wronged and we all want to do something, but generally in life we can’t do anything about it and we’re powerless.”
As EW points out, rather than having Matt haunted by his dad he instead weaponizes the memory of his father against his enemies. “He’s probably also saying, ‘No, I’m not my father,’” said Watkins.
For more on the film, read my Clayface review , our Clayface ending explained , and catch up on everything we know so far about the DCU’s Batman .

The missing link is a level of battery performance that can meet, if not beat, a comparable internal combustion engine, and the Finnish innovator Donut Lab has just taken a -30 degree Celsius step in that direction.
If the name Donut Lab rings a bell, run right out and buy yourself a cigar. CleanTechnica is among the many (many, many) EV enthusiasts following the Donut Lab story, which is a rather unusual one.

The company unveiled its new solid-state EV battery at the Consumer Electronics Show in January, describing it as “the world’s first solid-state battery that is ready for use in OEM vehicle manufacturing,” while also pledging to share the results of third-party testing.

“With a full charge in five minutes and 400 Wh/kg of energy density, it seemed too good to be true. However, for any skeptics out there, Donut Lab is posting a new video series along with supporting material that explains the results of an independent assessment at the VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland,” CleanTechnica reported in January.

That’s right, VTT has been validating Donut Labs’s claims every step of the way, and the startup has been sharing those reports, in excruciating detail. In a bit of clap-back at skeptics who are challenging its claims, Donut Lab directs the curious to the VTT reports on its website at I Donut Believe .

Donut Labs has kept VTT hopping since the big unveil. In March, VTT issued a report that validated the new battery’s performance at 100°C — in other words, the boiling point. That led some Donut-watchers, including CleanTechnica’s Christopher Arcus, to conclude that the battery is not based on lithium, as some others have surmised.

“Speculation that the Donut Lab battery is not real are diminishing as independent lab data shows 100° Celsius performance. Speculation that the battery may be lithium run[s] into difficulty explaining how a battery can work at 100° Celsius,” Arcus observed.

“In the independent tests, the thin membrane surrounding the pouch breached. If the contents were a standard lithium-ion with liquid electrolyte, there would have been significant outgassing and the organic electrolyte would have caught fire,” he further noted.

article_paragraphs: We’ve all known that the way the government classifies trucks and cars has been a bit of a moving target, so NHTSA is finally forcing trucks to actually do truck things.
The changes—which would reclassify today’s 70/30 truck-to-car ratio into a 30/70 situation—were made as part of the government’s loosening of MPG rules.
But the different rules for cars and trucks could mean that it will make sense to build a vehicle overseas and import it, given different rules for the domestic and imported fleets.
Some questions are difficult to answer. Is a hot dog a sandwich? Do crabs think fish can fly? Is a light truck a passenger car?

Whatever your responses are to the first two, the government made it clear that its legal answer to that last one will soon change. The announcement came in the Safer Affordable Fuel-Efficient (SAFE) Vehicles Rule III for Model Years 2022 to 2031 Passenger Cars and Light Trucks , which was published in the Federal Register at the end of September and goes into effect on November 30. While the change was made in the context of the Trump administration’s loosening of fuel-economy regulations, it might also force automakers to move some production outside the U.S., depending on the political winds.

The latest SAFE Rule updates fuel-economy standards for model years 2022 through 2031. Under the Biden administration, the standard had been set to a U.S. fleet average of around 50.4 mpg, but the new rules lower that to 34.9 mpg. Some of this change comes from new rules about what defines a car and what makes something a truck.

article_paragraphs: What I don’t know about Finland would fill a small library. As a fan of Formula One, I know that many Finnish surnames have multiple k’s — Mika Hakkinen, and Kimi Raikkonen, for example, not to mention World Rally driver Tommi Makkinen. In the world of motorsports, some like to say, “To finish first, you must first be Finnish.”

It’s also a great place to view the northern lights, and it tends to be cold there. Those low temperatures have attracted data center developers, because keeping warehouses full of computers cool is much easier to do when it is near freezing outside instead of broiling hot.

That is one reason why Google is planning to spend $13 billion building two new data centers in Finland. Things are not going well for Google, however. It started out with the slogan “Don’t be evil,” but has transitioned to being one of the largest invaders of personal space, as it helps governments around the world keep track of citizens who dare to think thoughts not sanctioned by official policy.

According to The Guardian , the company sparked outrage in Finland after it chopped down about 250,000 trees to make way for its data center in the town of Muhos on the border with Sweden. Then it was revealed it felled another 150,000 trees at another site in Otanmäki, which is located in the southern part of the country. Recently, the Finnish Licensing and Supervision Authority (LVV) ordered Google to stop work on both projects because it failed to complete the necessary environmental impact assessments before clearing the land.

Last week, Antti Järvinen, Google’s manager for operations in Finland, apologized for obliterating nearly 400,000 trees without permission, but claimed the company had acted “on the best understanding we had of the legislation at the time.” In other words, he played the Steve Martin card.

The furor over the trees has forced Finland to take a closer look at its permitting laws and procedures. To be fair, it’s economy is not as robust as some of its European neighbors, and the government had been working diligently to cut expenditures wherever possible. It has also been encouraging foreign investment.

When Google announced last month it was prepared to invest $13 billion in the country, prime minister Petteri Orpo said attracting investment was a “top priority” and “the value of the data economy extends far beyond direct investment”. He said the Google deal would “deliver lasting benefits for both parties.”

That’s what political leaders always say, but they seldom talk about the infrastructure costs associated with such economic opportunities. The people putting up the money expect airports, roads, schools, hospitals, and emergency services to be built by the local community, but they never offer to pay for those things, so the costs fall on the shoulders of local residents.

article_paragraphs: Marvel has reportedly cast Sandra Hüller in Avengers: Doomsday for a secret cameo role.

Information about the last-minute addition comes from The Hollywood Reporter , which said the Project Hail Mary star will appear on screens when Earth's Mightiest Heroes take on Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom this December. Although much of that cast and their parts in the movie have been confirmed, details about Hüller's role were not shared.

Marvel Studios and directors Joe and Anthony Russo almost certainly have plans for plenty of superhero moments and surprises. How Hüller fits into that plan remains to be seen, but considering fans had already speculated about her involvement in recent days, some of the less patient Marvel Cinematic Universe enjoyers are probably already doing their best to piece together Doomsday's mysteries early.

Hüller is a German actor with a decades-long career on movie and TV screens. She was nominated for Actress in a Leading Role at the 2024 Oscars for her part in Anatomy of a Fall, but is also known for her parts in films like Digger, The Zone of Interest, and Fatherland. If you missed her in any of those movies, there's a good chance you caught her playing Eva Stratt, a role that we called one of the best parts of Ryan Gosling's Project Hail Mary .

As for her Marvel introduction, all we know for now is that she'll appear in a cameo part, meaning she probably won't show up for much of its 2-hour-and-45-minute runtime . Like major stars – including Harry Styles and Charlize Theron – before her, it's possible that we could only see Hüller's character during a stinger moment shown during the film's credits sequence. There's at least little reason to suspect that's not on the table, especially considering Marvel will use Doomsday's plot to set up the release of Avengers: Secret Wars in December 2027.

Doomsday is out in just a few short months, but that clearly hasn't stopped Marvel from revealing new information for what's gearing up to be one of the year's biggest releases. Even more about the movie is expected to be revealed at the MLB World Series , which is just a few hours after this piece's publication. THR noted that the Russo brothers are knee-deep in post-production for the film ahead of its December 18, 2026, premiere.

Avengers: Doomsday will bring the Avengers, X-Men, Fantastic Four, and more when it arrives in a few months. Until then, you can read what Jeremy Renner had to say about the good guys' chances without Hawkeye . You can also see how David Harbour did his best to walk back what may have been an early spoiler .

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

article_paragraphs: Getting initial customers as a startup can be one of the most grueling challenges in business. Even when companies manage to snag some early interest, there’s no guarantee those customers will stick around.

At TechCrunch Disrupt last week, Elia Wallen, founder and CEO of travel startup Engine, Gamma founder and CEO Grant Lee, and Crystal Huang, general partner at Google Ventures, shared tips on how to attract and retain customers.

In the current era — when young AI companies like Cluely and Instinct are building big audiences not just through their products but also through their founders’ colorful online presences — social media can seem like a magic bullet for reaching early customers. But founders who want heighten their business strategy with modern marketing, have to be strategic, according to Lee.

Gamma, which sells AI-powered presentation software, managed to scale its business exponentially with a social media strategy that deployed influencers through its Ambassadors (or “Gambassador”) program. The company adopted the plan before influencer-based marketing was a tried-and-true strategy for smaller companies, eventually reaching a multi-billion dollar valuation .
But simply giving influencers a platform and telling them to promote your brand online doesn’t automatically translate to sales, said Lee. There’s more to it than that.

“If you have a product that can serve many different segments or use cases, then you want to basically have creators that can target each one of those,” Lee said. “If you have folks that are in consulting versus people that do all their marketing and create all the decks for their CMO, there’s all these different segments you might want to go after.”
Lee said sometimes founders seem to treat creator marketing or influencer marketing as a sort of set it and forget it thing.

“I think you’re better served by really spending a lot of time with these creators, because if they’re not able to understand how to articulate the value of your product, it doesn’t matter how much money you spend, it’s just going to fall flat,” Lee added.

article_paragraphs: On Friday, OpenAI said that it will train its models using cached copies and simulated versions of the internet instead of the live web because the models are too unpredictable to be trusted with live internet access.

The frontier lab announced its new policy two weeks after its rival, Anthropic, began limiting its newest and, in theory, most capable models from accessing the live internet. Researchers adopted these policies after months of incidents in which models pursuing training tasks broke into external systems in search of answers, collaborated on obscure message boards, and developed exotic hacking strategies.

“Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access,” the company said in a blog post .

OpenAI said that as recently as September 20, one of its frontier models exploited a misconfiguration to access the internet. That led the company to pause training work for the rest of the month so it could develop and test new approaches to securing its models.
The decision to train these models in sandboxes cut off from the internet is notable because employees at frontier labs have insisted that doing so would be nearly infeasible.

Keeping AI data centers separate from the internet “would need research teams to essentially be embedded inside of data centers in Iowa or wherever else around the world,” former OpenAI researcher Steven Adler told Fortune this month. “It’s a lot of overhead, and it isn’t clear to me that the safety benefits of it are large enough to merit just how large a tax it would be for a company to do it unilaterally.”

“In nearly every post I make on X, without fail, I get between five and ten comments about my inability to secure a sandbox, or asking why the hell we can’t just unplug the model from the internet,” an anonymous security engineer at OpenAI wrote in a September post on X. “These comments reflect a widening gap between where a lot of organizations and people are today and what the frontier labs are dealing with. There is also a general misunderstanding of how model training and evaluation work at these labs.”

The engineer, whose role has been confirmed previously by OpenAI, described how complex the training runs launched by OpenAI engineers are, noting that they require access a variety of resources and tools across many domains, and that thousands of researchers build, modify and test the environments. “So is it as easy as just putting it in a sandbox? No, it’s not,” he concluded.

article_paragraphs: GM has partnered with Peak Energy to develop next-generation sodium-ion battery cells, but they’re not going into EVs – they’re for grid-scale energy storage projects. GM Ventures is making a strategic investment in Peak Energy.

June 10, 2026: Under the partnership, GM will develop the sodium-ion cells in its Michigan battery labs and retain exclusive manufacturing rights. Peak Energy will integrate the cells into its battery storage systems as it ramps up US manufacturing.

The companies are targeting a market that’s growing rapidly as utilities add battery storage to support renewable energy, rising electricity demand, and the buildout of data centers and AI infrastructure.

Today’s stationary storage market is dominated by lithium-iron phosphate (LFP) batteries. But Peak Energy believes sodium-ion batteries can deliver a lower-cost alternative for grid applications, where energy density is less important than cost, reliability, and safety.

A key part of Peak’s pitch is its passively cooled battery storage platform. Conventional LFP battery systems require active cooling equipment to maintain safe operating temperatures, adding cost and complexity. Peak says its system eliminates those cooling systems entirely.
According to the company, its sodium-ion platform can reduce energy storage costs by 20% compared with conventional systems while delivering more than 99% uptime.

Peak also argues that its design wastes less energy. It estimates that replacing conventional LFP storage systems with its passively cooled technology could reduce annual battery-storage energy waste in the US by up to 2 terawatt-hours. That’s enough electricity to power a mid-sized city for a year.
GM’s vice president of battery and sustainability, Kurt Kelty, said sodium-ion is a strong fit for stationary storage.

title: What Can Grid Flexibility Actually Do Here?
raw_summary: Electricity-system flexibility has become an increasingly large bucket. Batteries go into it. Demand response goes into it. Virtual power plants, EV charging, interconnectors, hydro, thermal storage and grid-enhancing technologies all get described as flexibility too. Those resources can all be useful, but a national total of “flexible megawatts” does not tell a grid operator very much about whether a congested transformer can take another connection, whether an evening peak can be covered, or whether the system can get through several difficult days.

article_paragraphs: Electricity-system flexibility has become an increasingly large bucket. Batteries go into it. Demand response goes into it. Virtual power plants, EV charging, interconnectors, hydro, thermal storage and grid-enhancing technologies all get described as flexibility too.

Those resources can all be useful, but a national total of “flexible megawatts” does not tell a grid operator very much about whether a congested transformer can take another connection, whether an evening peak can be covered, or whether the system can get through several difficult days.

I’ve published a new open 99-page TFIE Strategy report, The Flexibility Mesh: A Whole-System Architecture for Reliable, Affordable Electrification , to put those different jobs into one common architecture.

The animation runs the same underlying electricity system through four operating moments. During renewable-surplus midday, useful actions can include charging batteries and EVs, heating water, increasing some industrial loads and exporting electricity where there is somewhere useful for it to go. Move into an evening or winter peak and batteries discharge, some charging can pause, buildings can use heat stored earlier, hydro can increase output and industrial demand may reduce within its operating constraints.

A local network constraint creates a different problem again. An overloaded transformer does not care that there are thousands of megawatts of flexible capacity somewhere else in the country. The resource has to be electrically relevant to that part of the network. Storage, managed charging, operating measures and eventually reinforcement can all have roles, but they have to be compared against the actual constraint.

Prolonged multi-day stress changes the portfolio once more. Response speed remains useful, but duration, replenishment and correlated availability become much more important. A resource that can respond beautifully for two hours does not acquire three days of stored energy simply because it is fast.

This is why the report treats flexibility as a system property rather than a technology category. Different jobs require different resources, locations and durations, while grid expansion and operational flexibility are complementary rather than competing philosophies.

That distinction is easy to lose in technology-led discussions. A battery can be excellent at intraday shifting while being irrelevant to a voltage problem at the wrong node. An interconnector can provide valuable balancing and energy exchange but needs evidence that supply will be available at the other end during the hours for which planners want to rely on it. Industrial loads can be highly controllable while remaining unavailable at particular times because production still has to happen.
